topics.label: What you want to build
topics.question: What should this system help someone do?
topics.beginner: For example: help support staff find answers in company documents, or warn engineers before equipment fails.
topics.why: It decides which kind of AI system fits and what to sketch first.

topics.label: Who uses it, and how much
topics.question: Who will use this system?
topics.beginner: For example: 50 support staff, your engineering team, or customers on your website. An approximate number helps us choose capacity.
topics.why: Usage drives cost and how much the system must scale.
topics.ifUnsure: About 100 users making 10 requests a day, for a first estimate.

topics.label: Information it uses
topics.question: Which information should the system use?
topics.beginner: For example: policy PDFs in SharePoint, customer records, application logs or sensor readings. Tell me where that information is stored today if you know.
topics.why: Data location and sensitivity shape security, storage and where it can run.
topics.ifUnsure: Internal business documents, no personal data, stored with the current provider.

topics.label: Cloud preference
topics.question: Do you already use a cloud provider, or have a preference?
topics.beginner: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or IBM — or “no idea”, and I'll suggest one based on what you already use.
topics.why: It sets which services we design with and which prices apply.
topics.ifUnsure: No preference yet; the design stays provider-neutral until we compare options.

topics.label: Systems it connects to
topics.question: Which existing tool should this system connect to first?
topics.beginner: For example: your website, Salesforce, Microsoft Teams or a ticketing system. You can say “none for the first version”.
topics.why: Integrations add components, permissions and failure points.
topics.ifUnsure: Standalone at first, with no integrations.

topics.label: How good, fast and safe
topics.question: What is the most important rule this system must meet?
topics.beginner: For example: “answers within 5 seconds”, “data stays in Australia”, or “a person approves replies before customers receive them”. We can add more rules afterwards.
topics.why: These become measurable requirements the review checks the design against.
topics.ifUnsure: Answers within 10 seconds, available in business hours, a person reviews anything sent outside the organisation.

topics.label: Budget and timeline
topics.question: How much could you spend each month to run this system in the cloud?
topics.beginner: Include the currency if you have a limit—for example, “AUD 100–300 per month”. This covers cloud services and AI usage, not the one-off cost of building it. If you do not know yet, say “estimate it for me”. We can discuss the target launch date separately.
topics.why: It tells us when an option is too expensive and what to build first.
topics.ifUnsure: No fixed budget; we'll estimate and you decide.
